evidence:
Trace identifies the registration codemode exposure runtime command and role-boundary integration points: `packages/integrations/pi/src/extension.ts:142-158,622-639,1651-1657` detects child sessions and gates excluded nested calls; `packages/integrations/pi/src/bash.ts:212` and `packages/integrations/pi/src/codex.ts:241` register bash and apply_patch, not HolyAgent CLI tools. Pi `docs/extensions.md` Tool Exposure and `docs/codemode.md` specify `registerTool`, `exposure: "codemode"`, discovery via `ALL_TOOLS`/`searchTools`/`describeTool`, and nested validation and `tool_call` events. `packages/runtime/src/cli/program.ts:56-88,110-179` resolves state, parses arguments, runs command Effects with `WorkTree`, and formats TOON or errors; `packages/runtime/src/cli/types.ts:61-122` supplies strict input decoding and state updates.
Recommendation covers every CLI functionality with tests and preserves CLI compatibility and approval boundaries: Inventory against `packages/runtime/src/cli/commands.ts:14-25`: intent create/show/list/update/close/reopen/use; assignment create/dispatch/record/close/accept/reports/show/list; plan/status/reconcile; migrate; setup/doctor; state mode; rg/fd; browser-server; vcs commit/identity/pr; hooks; help/version. Give each an explicit structured mapping or documented host-only equivalent: Pi FFF for rg/fd, lifecycle adapters for hooks/server, UI-aware setup, and metadata for help/version; do not silently omit them. Retain CLI and its checks; reuse command-level validation and VCS services (`packages/runtime/src/vcs/commands.ts:48-165`), not direct unchecked state mutations. Enforce specialist read-only access on structured mutations and existing root exclusions on nested calls; never treat an argument as proof of user approval. Test registry coverage, CLI/tool parity including errors and state modes, codemode discovery/direct and nested gates, specialist denials, approval denial/no-UI, concurrent mutations, cancellation, output and Bun/Node packaging; extend `packages/integrations/pi/tests/extension.test.ts:2928-2963` and `packages/runtime/tests/cli.test.ts`.
trace: Pi script `tools.holyagent_*({...})` → Pi schema validation and nested `tool_call` → role/approval gate → adapter → shared command operation and Effect services → state/VCS or host effect → structured result; errors must reject as tool failures and writes must be serialized because codemode can run parallel calls without rollback. Pi schema coercion and non-enforced TypeBox refinements require runtime validation after hooks mutate arguments.
options: 1. Preferred: named typed tools grouped by domain, shared command operations and validated schemas; discoverable and auditable, but requires extracting Bun-dependent or CLI-only paths. 2. One typed discriminated command tool backed by the same operation layer; fewer registrations but larger schema and coarser permission visibility. 3. Structured tools invoking bundled Bun CLI without a shell; preserves runtime behavior but adds process/TOON overhead and awkward streaming/server handling.

contract-sketch: Register `holyagent_intent`, `holyagent_assignment`, `holyagent_overview`, `holyagent_state`, `holyagent_vcs`, and explicit setup/migration/host adapters under a `holyagent` namespace, `exposure: "codemode"`; each takes a strict action-discriminated object with typed fields, returns `outputSchema`/`structuredContent` plus model-facing `content`, and throws mapped tagged errors with hints. Use per-operation names instead where a group’s approval or schema cannot be safely distinguished; pass `ctx.cwd` and abort signal, and serialize state mutations.
